claim: The bacterial flagellar motor switches rotational direction between counterclockwise (CCW) and clockwise (CW) to direct the migration of the cell.
source: The bacterial flagellar motor switches rotational direction between counterclockwise (CCW) and clockwise (CW) to direct the migration of the cell.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific knowledge about bacterial flagellar motors.

claim: The cytoplasmic ring (C-ring) of the motor is composed of FliG, FliM, and FliN.
source: The cytoplasmic ring (C-ring) of the motor, which is composed of FliG, FliM, and FliN, is known for controlling the rotational sense of the flagellum.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the composition of the C-ring, supported by prior research.

claim: The C-ring is known for controlling the rotational sense of the flagellum.
source: The cytoplasmic ring (C-ring) of the motor, which is composed of FliG, FliM, and FliN, is known for controlling the rotational sense of the flagellum.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the function of the C-ring.

claim: The C-ring maintained 34-fold symmetry in both rotational senses.
source: We report that the C-ring maintained 34-fold symmetry in both rotational senses, and the protein composition remained constant.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the cryo-ET data presented in the manuscript, shown in Figure 1C,F.

claim: The protein composition of the C-ring remained constant between CCW and CW rotation.
source: We report that the C-ring maintained 34-fold symmetry in both rotational senses, and the protein composition remained constant.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that both structures have 34-fold symmetry and similar diameters at the middle and bottom regions.

claim: FliG conformational changes elicit a large conformational rearrangement of the rotor complex that coincides with rotational switching of the flagellum.
source: The two structures show FliG conformational changes elicit a large conformational rearrangement of the rotor complex that coincides with rotational switching of the flagellum.
evidence: This is a primary finding based on comparison of the two structures determined by cryo-ET.

claim: FliM and FliN form a stable spiral-shaped base of the C-ring.
source: FliM and FliN form a stable spiral-shaped base of the C-ring, likely stabilizing the C-ring during the conformational remodeling.
evidence: This is based on structural observations from the cryo-ET maps showing continuous helical density at the base.

claim: The FliM-FliN spiral likely stabilizes the C-ring during the conformational remodeling.
source: FliM and FliN form a stable spiral-shaped base of the C-ring, likely stabilizing the C-ring during the conformational remodeling.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation based on the observation that the spiral remains uniform in both rotational states.

claim: Escherichia coli and Salmonella enterica use a 'run-and-tumble' approach for controlling movement.
source: Escherichia coli and Salmonella enterica (henceforth, Salmonella) use a 'run-and-tumble' approach for controlling movement, by which flagella rotating in a CCW sense drive the cell body forward, and when the rotation sense switches to CW the bacterium tumbles through the medium to change direction (Berg, 2003; Chevance and Hughes, 2008; Terashima et al., 2008).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations to prior research.

claim: In E. coli and Salmonella, flagella rotating in a CCW sense drive the cell body forward.

evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: When the rotation sense switches to CW, E. coli and Salmonella tumble through the medium to change direction.

evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Vibrio alginolyticus has a unique three-step swimming pattern with forward, reverse, and flick motions.

evidence: This is established knowledge about V. alginolyticus motility supported by citation.

claim: In V. alginolyticus, CCW rotation propels the cell body forward.

claim: FliGM holds the upper, membrane-proximal portion of the C-ring in contact with its lower, membrane-distal portion.

evidence: This is inferred from the structural observations.

claim: The middle and bottom regions of the C-ring are similar in diameter between CCW and CW motors.
source: The protein composition of the C-ring likely remains the same as both CCW- and CW-motors have 34-fold symmetry, and the middle and bottom regions of the C-ring are similar in diameter.
evidence: This is an observation from the cryo-ET data.

claim: The C-ring subunit was built with FliG at the top, FliM in the middle, and three FliN molecules at the base.
source: We built the C-ring subunit with FliG at the top, FliM in the middle, and three FliN molecules at the base (see Figure 2C,F for clarification), supporting the 1:1:3 (FliG, FliM, and FliN) model in lieu of the 1:1:4 model, as there is no additional density for a fourth FliN molecule.
evidence: This is a description of the model building based on the cryo-ET data.

claim: The data support the 1:1:3 (FliG, FliM, and FliN) model in lieu of the 1:1:4 model.
source: We built the C-ring subunit with FliG at the top, FliM in the middle, and three FliN molecules at the base (see Figure 2C,F for clarification), supporting the 1:1:3 (FliG, FliM, and FliN) model in lieu of the 1:1:4 model, as there is no additional density for a fourth FliN molecule.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the absence of density for a fourth FliN in the cryo-ET map.

claim: There is no additional density for a fourth FliN molecule.
source: We built the C-ring subunit with FliG at the top, FliM in the middle, and three FliN molecules at the base (see Figure 2C,F for clarification), supporting the 1:1:3 (FliG, FliM, and FliN) model in lieu of the 1:1:4 model, as there is no additional density for a fourth FliN molecule.
evidence: This is an observation from the cryo-ET data.

claim: The CCW subunit has a CCmask of 0.69 and CCbox of 0.83.
source: From this patch model single subunit was real space rigid body refined with the CCW subunit having CCmask of 0.69, and CCbox of 0.83 and the CW subunit had a CCmask of 0.66 and CCbox of 0.82 (Figure 3A,C).
evidence: This is a quantitative measure of model fit to the cryo-ET data.

claim: The CW subunit has a CCmask of 0.66 and CCbox of 0.82.
source: From this patch model single subunit was real space rigid body refined with the CCW subunit having CCmask of 0.69, and CCbox of 0.83 and the CW subunit had a CCmask of 0.66 and CCbox of 0.82 (Figure 3A,C).
evidence: This is a quantitative measure of model fit to the cryo-ET data.

claim: The continuous helical density at the base of the C-ring is the same as shown in Salmonella.
source: We observed the same continuous helical density at the base of the C-ring as shown in Salmonella (Thomas et al., 2006) and proposed to be formed via alternating FliMC-FliN heterodimers and FliN homodimers (McDowell et al., 2016) connecting adjacent subunits (Figure 4A,B).
evidence: This is an observation from the cryo-ET data compared to prior research.

claim: The spiral is proposed to be formed via alternating FliMC-FliN heterodimers and FliN homodimers connecting adjacent subunits.
source: We observed the same continuous helical density at the base of the C-ring as shown in Salmonella (Thomas et al., 2006) and proposed to be formed via alternating FliMC-FliN heterodimers and FliN homodimers (McDowell et al., 2016) connecting adjacent subunits (Figure 4A,B).
evidence: This is a model from prior research that is consistent with the current data.

claim: The MCN3 spiral is uniform within both the CCW and CW cryo-ET maps.
source: This region, known as a spiral (McDowell et al., 2016), is uniform within both the CCW and CW cryo-ET maps, and remains largely unaltered upon rotational switching (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is an observation from comparing the two cryo-ET structures.

claim: The MCN3 spiral remains largely unaltered upon rotational switching.
source: This region, known as a spiral (McDowell et al., 2016), is uniform within both the CCW and CW cryo-ET maps, and remains largely unaltered upon rotational switching (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is an observation from comparing the two cryo-ET structures.

claim: The MCN3 spiral is important for keeping the C-ring subunits connected during the conformational remodeling and rotation.
source: Taken together, these data suggest that perhaps the MCN3 spiral is important for keeping the C-ring subunits connected during the conformational remodeling and rotation.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation based on the observation that the spiral remains stable.

claim: There is a 23 Å shift of FliG with a 37° tilt about FliM.
source: Using UCSF Chimera (Pettersen et al., 2004) an axis was drawn through the center of the model, FliGMC shown in red, FliGMC and FliMM in green, and FliMM alone in orange. This revealed a 23 Å shift of FliG with a 37o tilt about FliM (Figure 3—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is a measurement from comparing the CCW and CW models.

claim: FliG and FliM tilt 20° outward upon switching from CCW to CW rotation.
source: FliG and FliM tilt 20o outward upon switching from CCW to CW rotation (Figure 3—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is a measurement from comparing the CCW and CW models.

claim: The large conformational change can be attributed to FliMM.
source: Furthermore, comparison of just the axes shows that the movement characterizing the large conformational change can be attributed to FliMM (Figure 3—figure supplement 3 insets).
evidence: This is an inference from the structural analysis.

claim: FliG is presumably presented to the stator units very differently as a result of the rearrangement of FliMM.
source: This suggests that, upon switching, FliG is presumably presented to the stator units very differently as a result of the rearrangement of FliMM.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation based on the observed conformational changes.

claim: An extra ring is observed around the CW-locked C-ring.
source: We observed an extra ring around the CW-locked C-ring (Figure 2).
evidence: This is an observation from the cryo-ET data shown in Figure 2.

claim: The extra density around the CW C-ring is speculated to be formed by CheY-P.
source: We speculate that it is formed by CheY-P, as there are several pieces of evidences in line with this model.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation based on multiple lines of reasoning.

claim: The density is above the noise level in the CW-motors but not in the CCW-motors.
source: First, the density is above the noise level in the CW-motors but not in the CCW-motors, which biochemically makes sense as CheY-P binds to CW rotating motors (Paul et al., 2011; Vartanian et al., 2012; Dyer et al., 2009; Lee et al., 2001b).
evidence: This is an observation from the cryo-ET data.

claim: CheY-P binds to CW rotating motors.
source: First, the density is above the noise level in the CW-motors but not in the CCW-motors, which biochemically makes sense as CheY-P binds to CW rotating motors (Paul et al., 2011; Vartanian et al., 2012; Dyer et al., 2009; Lee et al., 2001b).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Density similar in location and shape has been shown in two recent studies to be CheY-P.
source: Second, density similar in location and shape has been shown two recent studies to be CheY-P. Chang et al. have used GFP-tagged CheY-P to show that, in Borrelia burgdorferi, CheY-P occupies the same position (Chang et al., 2020). Rossmann et al. also identified similar density for the CheY homolog, CleD in Caulobacter crescentus (Rossmann et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supporting evidence from recent studies cited.

claim: There is about 60 Å gap between the C-ring density and the additional density when CheY is placed into the model.
source: Third, when we place the crystal structure of CheY into the model, there is about 60 Å gap between the C-ring density and this additional density (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a measurement from the model.

claim: The 60 Å distance may be bridged by the 42 residues of FliMN to connect CheY-P to FliMM.
source: This distance may be bridged by the 42 residues of FliMN to connect CheY-P to FliMM.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation based on the structural model.

claim: The C-ring possesses two distinct conformations in CCW and CW rotation.
source: The flagellar motor structures we determined provide direct evidence that the C-ring possesses two distinct conformations in CCW and CW rotation.
evidence: This is a primary conclusion from the cryo-ET structures.

claim: The dynamics of the C-ring appear to be confined to the upper two-thirds of the structure.
source: The dynamics of the C-ring appear to be confined to the upper two-thirds of the structure, with the spiral base that connects the C-ring subunits remaining relatively static.
evidence: This is an inference from the structural observations.

claim: The spiral base that connects the C-ring subunits remains relatively static.
source: The dynamics of the C-ring appear to be confined to the upper two-thirds of the structure, with the spiral base that connects the C-ring subunits remaining relatively static.
evidence: This is an observation from comparing the two structures.

claim: A 37° lateral and 20° medial tilting of the C-ring was observed.
source: We observed a 37o lateral and 20o medial tilting of the C-ring (Figure 3—figure supplement 3), which almost certainly alters its interactions with the stator.
evidence: This is a measurement from the structural analysis.

claim: The tilting of the C-ring almost certainly alters its interactions with the stator.
source: We observed a 37o lateral and 20o medial tilting of the C-ring (Figure 3—figure supplement 3), which almost certainly alters its interactions with the stator.
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on the observed conformational changes.

claim: The charged residues (Lys284, Arg301, Asp308, and Asp309 in FliGC) that interact with the stator are located at the top of the C-ring.
source: In our pseudo-atomic model, the charged residues (Lys284, Arg301, Asp308, and Asp309 in FliGC) that are known to interact with the stator are located at the top of the C-ring.
evidence: This is a description of the model based on known interactions.

claim: FliGC moves about 40 Å laterally.
source: FliGC moves about 40 Å laterally (Video 1).
evidence: This is a measurement from the structural comparison.

claim: The large remodeling of the C-ring presumably enables distinct interactions between the stator and the C-ring.
source: This large remodeling of the C-ring presumably enables distinct interactions between the stator and the C-ring (Video 2).
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation based on the observed conformational changes.

claim: A flexible linker attaching FliGCN and FliGCC would allow for a range of movement in FliGCC relative to FliGCN and FliGM.
source: A flexible linker attaching the two domains would allow for a range of movement in FliGCC relative to FliGCN and FliGM, thus suggesting that the presentation of the charged residues varies greatly depending upon the conformation of FliG.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation based on the structural model.

claim: The presentation of the charged residues varies greatly depending upon the conformation of FliG.
source: A flexible linker attaching the two domains would allow for a range of movement in FliGCC relative to FliGCN and FliGM, thus suggesting that the presentation of the charged residues varies greatly depending upon the conformation of FliG.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation based on the structural model.

claim: The C-ring has 34-fold symmetry in both the CCW and CW rotating C-rings.
source: Notably, our cryo-ET model shows 34-fold symmetry for both the CCW and CW rotating C-rings, with only a modest diameter change in FliG.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the cryo-ET data.

claim: There is only a modest diameter change in FliG between CCW and CW rotation.
source: Notably, our cryo-ET model shows 34-fold symmetry for both the CCW and CW rotating C-rings, with only a modest diameter change in FliG.
evidence: This is an observation from the cryo-ET data.

claim: It has been hypothesized that the FliG, FliM, and FliN composition of the C-ring changes during rotational switching.
source: It has previously been hypothesized, based on experiments utilizing fluorescently tagged FliM and FliN, that the FliG, FliM, and FliN composition of the C-ring changes during rotational switching (Delalez et al., 2014; Delalez et al., 2010; Hosu and Berg, 2018; Lele et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a prior hypothesis from the literature supported by citations.

claim: A recent single-particle cryo-EM study suggested that inter-subunit spacing and interactions of the C-ring account for motor switching in Salmonella.
source: A recent single-particle cryo-EM study suggested that inter-subunit spacing and interactions of the C-ring account for motor switching in Salmonella (Sakai et al., 2019).
evidence: This is a prior finding from the literature supported by citation.

claim: A prior study reported a 9 Å decrease in C-ring diameter upon switching to CW.
source: That study reported a 9 Å decrease in C-ring diameter upon switching to CW.
evidence: This is a prior finding from the literature.

claim: The current study reports identical diameters at the middle of the C-ring in both rotational directions.
source: We report identical diameters at the middle of the C-ring in both rotational directions.
evidence: This is a finding from the current cryo-ET data.

claim: The current study observed ~21 Å increase in the diameter at FliGC of the CW-motor.
source: However, we observed ~21 Å increase in the diameter and ~40 Å lateral change at FliGC of the CW-motor.
evidence: This is a finding from the current cryo-ET data.

claim: The current study observed ~40 Å lateral change at FliGC of the CW-motor.
source: However, we observed ~21 Å increase in the diameter and ~40 Å lateral change at FliGC of the CW-motor.
evidence: This is a finding from the current cryo-ET data.

claim: Chang et al. used a B. burgdorferi with a CheX deletion or CheY3 deletion to investigate the switching mechanism of spirochetes.
source: In a parallel study, Chang et al. used a B. burgdorferi with a CheX deletion or CheY3 deletion to investigate the switching mechanism of spirochetes (Chang et al., 2020).
evidence: This is a description of a parallel study supported by citation.

claim: Similar conformational changes of the C-ring were observed in both V. alginolyticus and B. burgdorferi.
source: Similar conformational changes of the C-ring were observed in both species; however, the stator complexes were resolved in B. burgdorferi, as they appear to be less dynamic than those in V. alginolyticus.
evidence: This is a comparison with a parallel study.

claim: The stator complexes were resolved in B. burgdorferi because they appear to be less dynamic than those in V. alginolyticus.
source: Similar conformational changes of the C-ring were observed in both species; however, the stator complexes were resolved in B. burgdorferi, as they appear to be less dynamic than those in V. alginolyticus.
evidence: This is an inference from comparing the two studies.

claim: Visualization of the stator complex in B. burgdorferi provided direct evidence that the conformational change of the C-ring alters the rotor-stator interaction.
source: Visualization of the stator complex provided direct evidence that the conformational change of the C-ring alters the rotor-stator interaction.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the parallel study.

claim: Santiveri et al., 2020 postulated that MotA rotates CCW in Campylobacter jejunie.
source: Santiveri et al., 2020 further postulated that MotA rotates CCW in Campylobacter jejunie by showing that the conformations of wildtype MotAB and MotAB trapped in the protonated state are nearly identical, thus ruling out a dramatic conformational change in the stator unit.
evidence: This is a finding from a cited study.

claim: The conformations of wildtype MotAB and MotAB trapped in the protonated state are nearly identical.
source: Santiveri et al., 2020 further postulated that MotA rotates CCW in Campylobacter jejunie by showing that the conformations of wildtype MotAB and MotAB trapped in the protonated state are nearly identical, thus ruling out a dramatic conformational change in the stator unit.
evidence: This is a finding from a cited study.

claim: The change in rotational direction occurs from a large movement of the charged residues of FliGC relative to the stator.
source: Therefore, we conclude that the change in rotational direction occurs from a large movement of the charged residues of FliGC relative to the stator.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the current data and cited studies.

claim: The in situ structures support that FliG, FliM, and FliN interact in a 1:1:3 ratio.
source: Our in situ structures support that FliG, FliM, and FliN interact in a 1:1:3 ratio, as suggested for the non-flagellar homolog Spa33 in Shigella (McDowell et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a conclusion from the current structural data compared to prior research.

claim: FliM holds the individual C-ring subunits together by interacting with FliGM and forming a heterodimer with FliN.
source: This stoichiometry favors the model in which FliM holds the individual C-ring subunits together by interacting with FliGM and forming a heterodimer with FliN.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the structural model.

claim: The FliM-FliN spiral connects adjacent C-ring subunits, allowing for dramatic movement without dissociation of the subunits.
source: The FliM-FliN spiral connects adjacent C-ring subunits, allowing for dramatic movement without dissociation of the subunits.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the structural observations.

claim: The FliGM-FliMM interface has been suggested to be involved in flagellar switching.
source: The FliGM-FliMM interface, perhaps dynamic in its own right, has been suggested to be involved in flagellar switching (Sakai et al., 2019; Dyer et al., 2009; Pandini et al., 2016).
evidence: This is established knowledge from prior research supported by citations.

claim: NMR showed that CheY-P binding to FliM displaces FliGC.
source: It was shown, using NMR, that the CheY-P binding to FliM displaces FliGC, and that the dramatic rearrangement of FliGMC is possible because of the flexibility of FliG (Dyer et al., 2009).
evidence: This is a finding from prior research supported by citation.

claim: The dramatic rearrangement of FliGMC is possible because of the flexibility of FliG.
source: It was shown, using NMR, that the CheY-P binding to FliM displaces FliGC, and that the dramatic rearrangement of FliGMC is possible because of the flexibility of FliG (Dyer et al., 2009).
evidence: This is a finding from prior research supported by citation.

claim: The GGPG loop in FliMM is suggested to be critical for rotation of FliGM relative to FliMM.
source: In particular, the GGPG loop in FliMM is suggested to be critical for rotation of FliGM relative to FliMM (Pandini et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a finding from prior research supported by citation.

claim: Point mutations targeting FliMM were shown to restore CCW rotation in a CW-biased mutant.
source: Most recently, point mutations targeting FliMM were shown to restore CCW rotation in a CW-biased mutant (Sakai et al., 2019).
evidence: This is a finding from prior research supported by citation.

claim: The conformational change in FliG results in a rotation about FliMM that leads to the tilting of the C-ring subunit.
source: These results, combined with our findings, lead us to suggest that the conformational change in FliG results in a rotation about FliMM that leads to the tilting of the C-ring subunit to alter the presentation of the charged residues of FliGC to the stator.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the current data and prior research.

claim: The putative CheY-P-ring is likely associated with the CW C-ring.
source: Given that the putative CheY-P-ring is likely associated with the CW C-ring (Figure 1), we propose a CCW-to-CW switching model (Figure 5, Videos 1 and 3).
evidence: This is based on the observation of extra density in the CW motor.

claim: CheY-P binding to FliM results in a conformational change in FliG and alters the interactions between the C-ring and stator.
source: CheY-P binding to the FliM results in a conformational change in FliG and alters the interactions between the C-ring and stator.
evidence: This is a proposed mechanism based on the structural data and prior knowledge.

claim: FliMC and FliN create a spiral base that holds the C-ring together during dynamic rearrangements.
source: FliMC and FliN create a spiral base that holds the C-ring together during these dynamic rearrangements.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the structural observations.

claim: FliMC and FliN may be involved in relaying the conformational change to adjacent C-ring subunits.
source: FliMC and FliN may also be involved in relaying the conformational change to adjacent C-ring subunits.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation based on the structural observations.

claim: Placing the FliG crystal structures of the open and closed variations within the cryo-ET image provides additional evidence to support the domain-swapping model.
source: By placing the FliG crystal structures of the open and closed variations within our cryo-ET image, we provide additional evidence to support the proposed model in which the ARMM and ARMC domains toggle between inter- and intramolecular interactions (Lee et al., 2010).
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the model building and prior research.

claim: NMR data suggest that FliGC is the domain that moves and that FliGM remains in stable contact with FliM.
source: NMR data suggest that FliGC is the domain that moves and that FliGM remains in stable contact with FliM (Dyer et al., 2009).
evidence: This is a finding from prior research supported by citation.

claim: Changes in the C-ring structure produce the two directions of flagellar rotation.
source: These changes in the C-ring structure produce the two directions of flagellar rotation.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the structural observations.

claim: Each V. alginolyticus cell usually possesses a single, polar, sheathed flagellum.
source: Each V. alginolyticus cell usually possesses a single, polar, sheathed flagellum, which limits the amount of information per cell for in situ motor structure determination.
evidence: This is established knowledge about V. alginolyticus.

claim: The fliG-G214S and fliG-G215A mutations were introduced into the flhG KK148 strain, which produces multiple flagella at the cell pole.
source: We therefore introduced the fliG-G214S and fliG-G215A mutations (Table 1) into the flhG KK148 strain, which produces multiple flagella at the cell pole (Kusumoto et al., 2006).
evidence: This is a description of the experimental approach.

claim: Tomograms were collected using a 300kV Titan Krios electron microscope with Volta phase plate, a GIF energy filter and a post-GIF K2 detector.
source: Tomograms were collected using a 300kV Titan Krios electron microscope (Thermo Fisher) with Volta phase plate, a GIF energy filter and a post-GIF K2 detector electron detector (Gatan).
evidence: This is a description of the data collection methods.

claim: 259 tomograms of CCW-state motor (G214S mutation) were generated.
source: In total, 259 tomograms of CCW-state motor (G214S mutation) and 220 tomograms of CW-state motor (G215A mutation) were generated.
evidence: This is a description of the data collected.

claim: 220 tomograms of CW-state motor (G215A mutation) were generated.
source: In total, 259 tomograms of CCW-state motor (G214S mutation) and 220 tomograms of CW-state motor (G215A mutation) were generated.
